sun.upright:
An Aries Sun is built to go first, and to be seen going. You'd struggle to find a less Aries card in the pack to draw for that part of you. It belongs to the Moon in Cancer, and Cancer sits square to Aries, three signs apart, both cardinal, both wanting to start things but by opposite methods. Aries starts by charging. Cancer starts by pulling back to check it's safe. The Moon has no standing in your sign either, so the card arrives as a guest in Mars's house, and a guest who wants to sit under a tree and think is not what Mars had planned for the day.

That's why this draw can feel like a flat tyre. The drive is still there, but the usual targets have lost their shine. You look at the three things you've already won, the job, the fitness goal, the argument, and feel oddly nothing about any of them. Fire and water don't mix easily, and when feeling floods a fire sign you get steam. Restless, irritable, bored, and a bit ashamed of being bored, because Aries Suns are meant to want things. I see this a lot in Aries charts after a big push. The body's done the sprint and the will hasn't caught up with the fact that it's over.

At work it's the promotion you chased that now looks like more of the same. In a relationship it's being short with your partner because they're happy and you're not sure what you're for. With your body it's the training plan you've quietly stopped. Before you pick the next target, spend a week saying no to new challenges. Notice which one you keep thinking about when nobody's asking.
sun.reversed:
Turned upside down for an Aries Sun, the card usually means the sulk has gone on too long and turned into a stance. You've decided nothing on offer is worth the effort, and Mars, who hosts the Moon in your sign, would sooner stay cross than admit to being flat. So you refuse things fast. The invitation, the idea a colleague floats, the offer of help. It looks decisive from outside. Inside it's mostly pride keeping you from reaching.

The other version is a lurch back into action with nothing behind it, a new project started just to feel the engine turn over. It tends to show up at work as dismissing the one proposal that was actually good because it wasn't yours. At home it's the partner who's stopped suggesting things. Pick one offer you turned down lately and go back to it. Ask whether you'd have said yes on a better day.

moon.upright:
The Moon in Aries needs to feel something fast and do something about it. That's how an Aries Moon settles, by moving. Drawing the Four of Cups for your tides is a strange fit, because this card's Moon is the Cancer Moon, at home and slow, sitting with a feeling until it's finished. Cancer squares Aries. The two ways of feeling rub against each other, and the square is the kind of friction that forces something to happen eventually, even if the first few days just feel stuck.

What this is like from the inside is boredom with a hot edge. The things that usually cheer you up, a run, a fight you can win, a new plan, don't touch it. You try one after another and each lasts about twenty minutes. Water and fire are opposed elements, and this is the water side winning for once, damping you down, and your fire doesn't know what to do with being damped. You'd honestly prefer to be angry. Anger at least moves.

In your body it's the heavy legs, the long sleep that doesn't refresh, the appetite that's gone odd. With a partner it's picking at them because picking is easier than admitting you feel low. With a parent it can be an old feeling of being told to stop fussing, the family that didn't have much time for sad. Let yourself be flat for a couple of days without trying to fix it. Go for a walk with no destination and no timing, and let it be slow.
moon.reversed:
With the card reversed, an Aries Moon may be fighting the low mood instead of feeling it. Mars rules your Moon's sign and the Moon has no rank here, so it takes Mars's orders, and the order is to push through. Busy days, a lot of noise, a temper that goes off over nothing. Underneath it the flatness hasn't moved. It's just being stepped over.

Sleep usually tells on it first, going short and choppy. Friends get the loud, fine version of you and wonder why you've cancelled twice. A partner gets snapped at. Stop for one evening with nothing planned. If the low feeling comes up, give it a name out loud, even a clumsy one like 'fed up', and see if the restlessness eases once it's been said.

rising.upright:
Look at the figure on the card, arms folded under a tree, eyes on the grass. Now put that on an Aries Ascendant, which normally comes into a room like it's been fired from something. People who know you will notice the change before you do. The Moon has no standing in Aries and takes its orders from Mars, but the card's Cancer Moon sits square to your rising sign, and the square shows up in how you're coming across. Quieter, slower to answer, less interested in the first move.

Your instinct at the door is still to go. What's happening is that the instinct fires and then nothing follows it. You say yes to the drinks and leave early. You open the email about the new role, feel nothing, and close it. From your side it feels like losing your edge. From the other side, strangers may find you easier to talk to than usual, because you're not charging at them, and that's worth noticing even if it doesn't feel like you.

In a new job it's the first week where you do your work and don't fight for anything, and people quietly relax. On a date it's the one where you're listening more and talking less, which surprises both of you. With a new neighbour or a new team it's letting them come to you for once. Pay attention to who approaches while you're sitting still. Those are the people to follow up.
rising.reversed:
An Aries rising with this card upside down can come across as sullen, and that's the part to watch. Mars wants to be first through the door, the Cancer Moon in the card wants to stay under its tree, and reversed, the stand-off shows on your face. Arms crossed, short answers, a no before the question's finished. You might think you look calm. People read it as a wall.

It shows up in a first meeting where you decided the other person was dull within a minute, and at work as the new colleague you haven't bothered with. It can also flip into a forced brightness that doesn't convince anyone. Next time you meet someone, uncross your arms and ask them one question you actually want the answer to. Then listen to the answer all the way to the end.

sun.upright:
The Moon is exalted in Taurus. That means it's an honoured guest in your sign, the planet at its most comfortable and well fed, and this is a Moon card. So for a Taurus Sun this draw lands on friendly ground. Cancer and Taurus are sextile, two signs apart, water and earth, and the two elements get on. Water gives earth something to grow. Earth gives water somewhere to stay. You're being handed a card about stillness, and stillness is something you're naturally good at.

The catch is contentment. A Taurus Sun wants a life that's solid and good to be in, and is proud of having built one. The card shows three full cups already lined up on the grass, and a person who's stopped tasting them. That's the risk for you. You've got the house, the routine, the dependable job, the people, and you can't tell whether you're satisfied or just settled. Fixed earth doesn't like asking. Asking might mean change, and change is expensive. So you keep enjoying things in a slightly dutiful way, and the pleasure goes a bit thin, and you put it down to being tired.

With money it's the savings account that's doing well and the one thing you've wanted to spend on for years. At work it's the role you're excellent at and have stopped learning in. In a relationship it's the comfortable Friday that's been the same Friday for three years. Change one of your fixed pleasures for a month. Different café, different walk, different recipe. See what you actually miss.
sun.reversed:
Reversed, this card on a Taurus Sun is comfort that's gone stale and been defended anyway. The Moon exalted in your sign makes you very good at looking after yourself, and upside down that turns into guarding what you've got against anything new. The offer is on the table and you don't even look at it, because looking might mean wanting, and wanting means moving.

At work it shows up as turning down the new project on principle. With money it can be the reverse, a spending streak that tries to buy back a feeling that's gone flat. The Moon's other foothold in Taurus is the Six of Pentacles decan, the card of giving and receiving, so sometimes the stuck point is help. Accept one offer of help you'd usually wave off, and let the other person do it their way.

moon.upright:
A Taurus Moon is the Moon exalted, and people who have it tend to know how to feel good. Warm bed, proper food, a garden, someone's hand. So drawing this card for your tides is an odd one. The card's own Moon is in Cancer, at home, and yours is in Taurus at its most honoured, which means the planet is strong in both places and on good terms with itself, sextile across the two signs. There's nothing wrong with your capacity to be comforted. It's that the comforts have gone a bit numb.

From the inside that's confusing. Everything that usually works is still there and you still do it, and it's like eating with a cold, the taste turned down. Water and earth hold each other well, so the mood doesn't lurch. It just sits. Fixed earth can sit for a long time. You may not even call it low. You'd call it quiet, or tired, and keep going through your usual pleasures in the same order.

In the body this can look like eating for comfort without enjoying it, or sleeping long and waking up heavy. With a partner it's affection given out of habit, and the evening you both notice nobody's really there. With home it's the room you keep meaning to change. Pick one of the senses and give it something new. A fruit you've never bought, music you wouldn't normally play, a different soap. Pay attention to whether anything lifts.
moon.reversed:
When the card reverses on a Taurus Moon, the retreat has usually gone physical. You've stayed in, stayed on the couch, kept to the same four meals, and the Moon, exalted in your sign, will make that feel entirely reasonable. It is comfortable. It's also shut the door on the people who were offering something else. Taurus is fixed, and once it's decided the outside world is a bother, it can hold that view for months.

You'll see it in friendships first, the invitations that have tapered off because you kept saying you were too tired. A partner may have stopped suggesting weekends away. Money can show it too, the delivery app doing a lot of your feeling for you. Say yes to one plan outside the house, a small one with an end time, and go even if the couch argues.

rising.upright:
Taurus rising already comes across as calm, unhurried, good to be around. With the Four of Cups drawn for your mask, add a layer of reserve on top. The Moon is exalted in your rising sign, so whatever mood is showing on your face tends to look settled and dignified, even a flat one. Strangers take you for content. You might just be switched off.

There's something useful in that. Cancer is sextile to Taurus, and the card's water softens your earth, so people find you easy company, unthreatening, and they tell you things. What's harder is that an Ascendant this steady doesn't signal when it's bored. You'll sit through the whole dinner, the whole pitch, the whole first date, perfectly pleasant, and nobody knows you decided in the first ten minutes that you weren't interested. The Moon also rules the middle ten degrees of Taurus, the Six of Pentacles decan, which is about what gets offered and what gets taken. Someone new is holding something out to you, and your pleasant face is hiding that you haven't noticed.

At work it's the colleague who keeps inviting you to lunch. In dating it's a person who likes you more than you've clocked. With money it's an offer, a rate, a better deal, sitting in your inbox. Go back through the last few new people you've met and ask yourself honestly which of them was offering something. Reply to that one.
rising.reversed:
Taurus rising with the card reversed can look stubborn to people who've only just met you. You've made up your mind early, you're polite about it, and you don't budge. The Moon exalted on your Ascendant keeps it gracious, but reversed, the calm turns into a closed door. People offer and you smile and don't take it. Fixed earth hates being rushed, and a first meeting can feel like a rush.

It tends to show up when someone new at work suggests a better way of doing a thing you've always done, and you say you'll think about it and don't. Socially it's staying with the same small group and letting new friendships wither for want of a reply. Answer the next new person within a day. Let them see you're interested, even if it's only a little.

sun.upright:
Gemini Suns want to be interested in everything, and to be seen as the one who's always got something new to say. Draw the Four of Cups for that and the first thing you'll feel is the interest switched off. Cancer and Gemini sit next to each other, a semi-sextile, neighbours with little in common. Gemini's air moves on quickly. The Cancer Moon of the card sits and stays. The Moon has no special rank in your sign, so it takes its colour from Mercury, your ruler, and the mood tends to come out as mental. Bored, not sad.

That boredom is worth taking seriously. A mutable air sign usually solves a flat patch by finding a new thing. New book, new person, new tab. Here the new things don't work. You scroll, you start the podcast, you text three people, and it's all the same noise. Water and air don't clash, they just have to be introduced, and what's being introduced is the feeling underneath the restlessness. You might find it's quite simple. You're tired, or you miss someone, or you're disappointed in how something turned out.

At work it's the job that used to be varied and now feels like the same four tasks. With friends it's the group chat you've muted. With a partner it's conversation that's become logistics, and you not saying you miss the old kind. Turn the phone off for one evening and sit somewhere without a screen. Let yourself be bored all the way through and see what turns up when it runs out.
sun.reversed:
A Gemini Sun with this card reversed is often running from the flatness, very fast. Mercury is your ruler, and the Moon, visiting Gemini, takes its style from it, so the escape is words and ideas. Four new plans in a week, a course half-started, lots of talk about what you'll do next. None of it touches the mood. It's a way of never sitting under the tree at all.

It turns up at work as enthusiasm for the next thing with nothing finished behind you, and in friendships as being great company and hard to reach. Before you start anything new, write down what you're hoping it'll make you feel. If you already know the answer, you can probably skip the project and go straight for the feeling.

moon.upright:
There's a person under a tree on this card, not talking to anyone, and for a Gemini Moon that's close to the hardest thing to do. Your feelings settle by being talked about. Mercury rules your Moon's sign, and the Moon has no dignity in Gemini, so it takes on Mercury's habit of processing through words and company. The card's Moon is the Cancer kind, which processes by going quiet and waiting. Neighbouring signs, next to each other on the wheel, and they barely understand each other.

What you'll probably notice is that talking isn't helping. You tell the story to your sister, then to a friend, then online, and each time it lands a little flatter. Air and water have to be introduced, and here the water is asking for a bit of time alone before the words come. That can be uncomfortable. Silence can make a Gemini Moon feel like something's wrong. Mostly what's wrong is small and ordinary, and it needs one quiet evening, and it'll say what it is if you let it.

Sleep often shows it, the mind busy at midnight, looking for input. With a partner it's the chat that fills every silence, and the silence that would actually help. With friends it's reaching out a lot and feeling oddly lonely afterwards. Try a slow walk with no headphones. Don't phone anyone on the way. Notice what you think about in the last ten minutes.
moon.reversed:
This card reversed on a Gemini Moon often looks like chatter covering a low mood. You're fine, you're busy, you've got a lot on, and the tone is a little too bright. Mercury, who rules your sign, keeps the words coming so nobody, including you, has to look at the flat bit underneath. Mutable air moves on before a feeling has finished, and that's the habit this card is picking up.

It tends to show up in the late night scroll and the messages sent at odd hours. Friends may notice you're everywhere and hard to actually reach. A partner may notice you change the subject whenever it gets close. Pick one friend who's good at quiet and spend an hour with them without much talking. A walk works. So does sitting in a car. Let the conversation be short.

rising.upright:
Gemini rising usually meets people at a clip, curious, funny, three questions in before they've sat down. This card slows the doorway right down. The Moon is only visiting Gemini, with no rank of its own, and it takes on Mercury's style, so it isn't that you've gone silent. You're still chatting. It's that the chat has gone a bit automatic, and people can hear it.

Cancer and Gemini are neighbours on the zodiac, the semi-sextile, and each has what the other lacks. The card's water brings in something your air usually skips, which is the mood of a room before anyone's said anything. You might find you're picking up more than usual in first meetings and saying less. That's disorienting for a Gemini rising. Your whole approach is built on quick contact, and here you are, lingering at the edge, not sure you want to go in. Strangers may read you as distracted or a bit sad. Some will find you more approachable because of it.

At a party it's standing in the kitchen, half listening. In a new job it's doing the introductions politely and not following up. On a date it's being charming on autopilot while thinking about something else. The next time you meet someone new, let yourself be quiet for the first few minutes and just listen. Ask the second question, the one that follows up on what they actually said.
rising.reversed:
With the card upside down, Gemini rising can come across as scattered and a bit unavailable. You're friendly, you're talking, and people get the feeling you've already left. Mercury rules your Ascendant and colours the Moon here, so the retreat hides behind conversation, lots of it, none of it quite landing. Or it flips, and you avoid new people altogether, which for your sign is unusual enough that friends notice.

It's the new contact who doesn't hear back, and the introduction you made and forgot. At work people may start to find you hard to pin to anything. In dating it's the three good first dates with three people and no second. Choose one new connection from the last month and give it a proper follow-up, a real message with a question in it, and wait for the reply.

sun.upright:
This is one of your own cards. The Four of Cups is the last ten degrees of Cancer, ruled by the Moon, and the Moon rules Cancer itself, so the planet is at home and the card belongs to your sign. It speaks with the landlord's voice. For a Cancer Sun, whose purpose is looking after what matters and being seen as the one who holds things together, this is a card about that person running out.

Cancer is cardinal, and people forget that about you. You start things. You start the family dinners, the check-in texts, the care rota, the group that meets on Thursdays. What this draw describes is the point where you look at everything you've built and feel nothing, and then the guilt of feeling nothing about people you love. Same element, water on water, and the card amplifies the sign both ways, including the Cancer habit of going into the shell. It's a very familiar place to you. It's also safe, and it's easy to stay there too long and call it resting.

At home it's the meal you cook on autopilot. At work it's being the reliable one and quietly wishing someone else would be for a change. With your mother, or whoever raised you, it can be the feeling of being tired of being the good one. Let somebody look after you, properly, for a whole day. Tell them what you'd like, specifically. Don't do the dishes afterwards.
sun.reversed:
For a Cancer Sun the reversed card is usually the shell with the door locked. The Moon at home in your sign makes the retreat very comfortable, and reversed, it stops being a rest and starts being a policy. You stop answering. You stop asking. You tell yourself people are better off without you bothering them.

Family is where it shows first. The call you've let ring out three times, the visit you keep putting off. At work it can look like quiet resentment, doing everything and letting nobody in. Or it goes the other way and you overdo the caring to cover the flatness, and you end up even more tired. Answer one message you've been avoiding. Short is fine. Somebody's been waiting to hear from you.

moon.upright:
The Moon in Cancer drawn onto a Cancer Moon. It's the planet at home, the card native to the sign, same element, the most amplified this pairing ever gets, and it's a lot. Whatever you usually feel, you'll feel it doubled. This is the shell card, the time after enough has happened that you need to stop taking anything else in, and your Moon knows that state better than any other.

The good version is that you know how to do this. You know you need a quiet weekend, a closed door, the familiar blanket, and you'll take it. The harder version is that Cancer's third decan is the most inward slice of an inward sign. Feeling pools and doesn't drain. Memory gets loud. You'll find old things turning up, a comment from years ago, a smell that brings back a house. You may not want company and may resent anyone who tries. People who love you will offer, and offer again, and you'll let it sit.

In the body it's a stomach that won't settle and sleep that comes in bursts. With a partner it's gratitude you can't quite feel and an offer of comfort you can't quite take. With family it's a mood you picked up at a visit and brought home with you. Take the retreat. Give it a limit, though, a date you'll ring one person back, and write that date down.
moon.reversed:
When the card turns over for a Cancer Moon, the quiet usually has either gone sour or snapped. The sour version is brooding, the same hurt replayed at night, every kind message read as not quite kind enough. The Moon rules your sign, so the mood runs the house, and reversed, it can run it for weeks. Sleep goes strange either way.

The snapped version is coming out of the shell all at once, and sometimes that means a flood of feeling at the wrong person. It tends to land on whoever's closest. A partner, a parent, a friend who asked an innocent question. Before you let it out, check who it's actually about. Then say the smallest true part of it to that person, and leave the rest for later.

rising.upright:
Cancer rising already reads a room from the edge before it steps in. With the Four of Cups on the mask, the Moon, your chart ruler, is showing up at home in its own card, and the edge is where you'll stay for a while. People are meeting a softer, more private version of you. Friendly enough, just not reaching.

What's worth knowing is that your chart ruler and the card's planet are the same, so the card isn't a visitor here. It's describing how your whole chart is choosing to meet the world, and it's chosen to be careful. Water on water means that when you're guarded, you're very guarded, and you might not notice how much. You tell yourself you'll go to the thing when you're more in the mood. You don't reply to the new person until you've worked out what they want. Meanwhile someone has already been kind to you once or twice and you haven't quite registered it.

At work it's a new manager who keeps checking in, and you reading it as surveillance when it's care. In friendship it's the neighbour who invited you over, and the invite you left unanswered. In a romance it's the person who's clearly interested while you wait for proof. Think of the last kindness a new person showed you. Go back and acknowledge it, even late, even with a two-line message.
rising.reversed:
Cancer rising with this card reversed can look like a sudden disappearance. You're warm on Monday and gone by Wednesday. The Moon ruling your Ascendant, reversed, turns the natural caution into full withdrawal, and the people you've just met don't know what they did. Usually they didn't do anything. You got tired and pulled the shell over.

This comes up in new friendships that stall after one lovely evening. At work it's being liked early and then being hard to find. In a new romance it's the unanswered text that the other person reads as a no. When you need to pull back, tell the other person you're pulling back. A single line will do, and it saves them guessing.

sun.upright:
Leo Suns shine by being generous and being seen being generous, and this card asks you to sit down in the shade for a bit. That's hard on a sign ruled by the Sun itself. The Four of Cups carries the Moon in Cancer, and Cancer is Leo's neighbour, the sign just before yours, a semi-sextile. Neighbours with little in common. The Moon has no standing in Leo, so here it borrows the Sun's colours, which means even your low mood wants an audience, or at least wants to be noticed by somebody.

From the inside this is the odd experience of the applause not landing. You did the thing, people loved it, and you went home and felt flat. Fire and water are opposed elements, and the Cancer water in this card dampens the Leo fire enough that you notice the heat's gone. For a sign that runs on warmth that's disconcerting, and pride makes it hard to say so. Leo is fixed, too, so you'll often carry on performing the old enthusiasm for weeks after it's left, because stopping would be admitting something.

At work it's the project you're known for, which you'd quietly like to hand to someone else. In love it's your partner's compliment bouncing off, and you feeling bad that it bounced. With children, yours or other people's, it can be losing interest in the games you used to lead. Stop performing one thing you've stopped enjoying. Tell one person you're taking a break from it, and see how they take it.
sun.reversed:
Upside down on a Leo Sun, the card often shows as a sulk in a very large room. You've withdrawn, and you'd quite like everyone to notice you've withdrawn. The Moon taking the Sun's colours in your sign makes even a low patch a bit theatrical. Or the pride goes the other way and you won't admit anything's wrong at all, and put on the whole show while feeling hollow underneath.

It shows at work as turning down the good offer because it wasn't grand enough, and at home as being generous to everybody except the person who asked you directly how you are. Pick the person you'd be most embarrassed to be low in front of. Tell them, briefly, that you've been flat. Leave it there.

moon.upright:
A Leo Moon needs warmth coming back. Being loved out loud, being made a fuss of, the feeling of being somebody's favourite. Drawn for your tides, this card turns the volume on that down. Here the card's Cancer Moon meets a Leo Moon, neighbouring signs, and the Moon has no dignity in Leo, so it takes its lead from the Sun, and the Sun wants to be lit up. Water and fire are at odds, and this card is water.

What it feels like is being offered affection and not being able to take it in. Somebody says something kind and it slides off. You can't quite work out why, because being appreciated is usually exactly what settles you. The best guess is that you've run down from giving. Leo Moons give a lot of warmth, often without asking for anything back, and then feel it privately when it doesn't come. This card is what happens after enough of that. You go quiet, you stop offering, and the people who love you notice the change before you do.

With a partner it's the evening where they're trying and you can't meet them. With a friend it's the party you'd usually host and haven't. In the body it's a tiredness around the chest and the shoulders, and sleep that doesn't restore much. Let someone make a small fuss of you, a meal, a card, a phone call, without deflecting. Say thank you and stop there.
moon.reversed:
Reversed, a Leo Moon under this card can dig in. You've been hurt by not being noticed, and now you won't be coaxed. The Sun, colouring the Moon in your sign, turns the withdrawal into a statement, and fixed fire can hold a statement a long time. Someone offers an olive branch and you decide it isn't enough.

It shows most with the people closest to you, a partner, a best friend, a sibling, and it usually takes the form of a coolness that says 'you should know why'. They may not. Sleep and appetite can both go off. Before the next time you're cool with someone, ask yourself whether you've ever actually told them what you wanted. If you haven't, tell them. Keep it short and warm.

rising.upright:
People expect Leo rising to arrive warm, bright and a bit of an event. With the Four of Cups on your Ascendant you're arriving dimmer, and they'll notice. The Moon has no rank in Leo and takes its tone from the Sun, your chart ruler, so the mood still shows up in style, but it's a quieter style. Sunglasses indoors, so to speak. People meet a Leo rising who isn't performing, and some of them find it a relief.

The rub is between the card and your instinct. Leo is fixed fire, and fire likes to be seen. The card's water is drawing you back from being seen, and you're tired of the entrance, the warm-up, the first joke. Cancer sits just behind Leo on the wheel, the sign that comes before the show, and the card is pulling you back towards it. That's where you'd like to be. You might feel guilty about it, as if people are owed the usual version.

In a new job it's letting someone else be the charming one in week one. At a party it's arriving late, leaving early, and finding the one real conversation of the night on the stairs. On a date it's showing up less polished, and the other person liking you more for it. When you meet someone new, skip the routine you usually open with. Say you're a bit tired, if you are. See what they do with the honesty.
rising.reversed:
Leo rising with the card reversed can come across as haughty when it's really just flat. You don't want to join in, and the Sun's style on your Ascendant makes not joining in look like a decision about other people. Arms folded, bored face, a slightly royal distance. Strangers take it personally. Or you overcorrect and force the old sparkle, and people can see the effort.

At work it's new colleagues deciding you're aloof in the first week. Socially it's turning down the invitation with a little too much flourish, so it sounds like a verdict on the party. On a first date it's the boredom showing when you only meant to be tired. Say what's true next time, that you're low on energy, and let people off the hook. Most of them will be relieved and a few will offer to help.

sun.upright:
The Four of Cups is a card about noticing, or failing to, and that's a Virgo Sun's home ground. You're here to be useful, to spot what needs doing and do it well, and to be seen as someone who gets it right. The card's Cancer Moon is sextile to Virgo, two signs apart, water and earth, friendly elements. The Moon has no rank in Virgo and takes its colour from Mercury, your ruler, so the card's withdrawal comes out in a Mercury way. You think about it. A lot.

What this looks like from the inside is a sort of dissatisfied audit. You look at what you've done, the three cups on the grass, and find the flaw in each. The job's fine but. The relationship's good but. The flat's nice but. None of it feels finished enough to enjoy. A sextile is an easy opening that still has to be used, and the opening here is that the card's water could soften the audit, if you let a feeling count as information instead of a mess to be tidied. Mutable earth wants to fix. Some of this isn't a fix job.

At work it's being bored by a job you're very good at and not letting yourself say so. With your body it's the routine that's gone mechanical, the same walk, the same meal plan, a bit joyless. With a partner it's noticing everything that's slightly off and not mentioning the thing that matters. Write down three things you've got that are good enough as they are. Leave them on the list without adding a 'but'.
sun.reversed:
A Virgo Sun with this card reversed tends to turn the flatness into a project. If you can just get the system right, the diet, the schedule, the inbox, the feeling will go away. It won't, and meanwhile it keeps you busy. With Mercury setting the Moon's tone in Virgo, the retreat gets very organised, and very lonely.

Where it shows is work, first, the extra hours doing things nobody asked for. Then home, where you're tidying around people instead of talking to them. The offer you're missing is usually a person asking if you're all right, and you answering with a list of what you've done. Next time someone asks, answer with how you feel. One word is enough to start with.

moon.upright:
Virgo Moons settle when things are in order. The kitchen clean, the week planned, the body looked after properly. Draw the Four of Cups here and the order is all still there, and it isn't settling anything. The card's Cancer Moon sits sextile to your Virgo Moon, water meeting earth, and the Moon is a visitor in Virgo, where it takes its tone from Mercury. So the mood arrives through the mind. You're not sad exactly. You're critical, a bit fed up, picky about small things.

That pickiness is worth listening to, because it's usually covering something. Earth and water get on well, and this card's water can make your earth fertile if you let the feeling in, but a Virgo Moon's first move is to manage it. You'll find a reason the low mood makes sense, you'll adjust your routine, you'll try the supplement. What you won't do easily is sit under the tree and let yourself be disappointed for an afternoon, without improving anything.

It shows in your digestion and your sleep, which are the usual places Virgo Moons store worry. With a partner it's correcting how they load the dishwasher when what you want is a hug. With a friend it's being helpful about their problem and not mentioning yours. Give yourself one evening with no improving in it. Eat something simple, watch something silly, and go to bed without checking anything.
moon.reversed:
When this card flips on a Virgo Moon, the low mood tends to go into worry. Mercury, colouring your Moon, starts looking for what's wrong, and with this card it finds plenty. A symptom to look up, a message to reread, a small mistake at work that gets bigger overnight. The retreat turns into checking.

It lands on the body first, as tension that sits in your stomach or jaw, and on sleep, which gets shallow. A partner may find you distant and irritable at the same time. Friends may get very practical help and very little of you. Choose one worry you've been checking and decide to stop checking it for three days. Write it on paper, fold it up, and put it somewhere you won't see it.

rising.upright:
Virgo rising meets the world carefully. Neat, observant, a bit reserved until it's worked out what's needed. Draw this card for your mask and it adds a folded-arms quality to that, and people might read you as unimpressed. The card's Moon has no rank in Virgo and takes Mercury's style, so the withdrawal looks like critical distance. You're assessing. You're not joining in.

Some of that is useful. The sextile between Cancer and Virgo is an easy link, and the card's water gives your first impressions a softer, more perceptive edge. You'll pick up what someone's feeling faster than usual. The trouble is you may not do anything with it. You notice the new colleague is nervous, you notice the host is stressed, and you keep your observations to yourself, and from the outside that looks like coolness. Mutable earth adapts, so part of you is ready to engage. The other part is waiting until it's sure it's worth it, and the waiting shows on your face.

At work it's the meeting where you had a useful thing to say and didn't. In a new friendship it's the person who's warm to you, and you being polite back and nothing more. On a date it's spotting every small awkwardness and forgetting to enjoy yourself. Next time you notice something kind to say, say it straight away. Don't edit it first.
rising.reversed:
Reversed, the card on a Virgo Ascendant can make you come across as fussy or cold. You've pulled back, and what people see is the correction, the raised eyebrow, the question about detail when they wanted enthusiasm. Mercury styling your Ascendant makes the retreat precise, and precision reads as judgement to someone who's just met you.

This shows up at work with new people who decide early that you're hard to please. It shows in dating as nerves disguised as standards. It can show at home as being short with the neighbour who only wanted a chat. Before the next first meeting, pick one thing you like about the person and tell them. Keep the critique for later, if it's still needed.

sun.upright:
Libra Suns are here to make things fair and pleasant and to be seen as the one who keeps the peace. The Four of Cups squares that. Cancer is square to Libra, both cardinal, both starting signs, and the friction is real. Cancer starts by withdrawing to feel safe. Libra starts by reaching out to someone else. This card is the Cancer instinct overriding yours, so for once you don't want to reach out. You'd like everyone to leave you alone and you feel terrible for wanting it.

There's a quieter link too. The Moon rules the first ten degrees of Libra, the decan of the Two of Swords, the blindfolded figure who won't choose. So if your Sun is early Libra, this card and that one are cousins, and both describe the same stuck place, where you can't decide what you want, so you stop looking. Venus rules Libra, and with the Moon a visitor here, the flatness has a Venusian flavour. Things aren't beautiful any more. Your clothes, your flat, your friends' company, all slightly dull. Water and air are neither friends nor enemies, and it'll take effort to get your feelings and your social sense talking again.

At work it's the diplomat role you've quietly stopped wanting. In love it's being unsure whether you're bored with your partner or bored with yourself. With friends it's the group plans you keep agreeing to and dreading. Cancel one social thing you don't want to do, honestly and kindly. Spend that evening alone, and notice whether you miss anybody.
sun.reversed:
A Libra Sun with the card upside down can get stuck being agreeable. You're flat underneath and pleasant on top, and the effort of the pleasant bit is wearing you out. The square from Cancer makes the gap between how you feel and how you're behaving more and more uncomfortable. Something has to give, and usually it's your temper, at a bad moment, over something small. The Two of Swords, the Moon's own decan in Libra, knows this state well, the blindfold on so you don't have to see the choice.

This tends to show in a relationship where you've said 'I don't mind' so often you no longer know if you mind. At work it's the colleague you've been too nice to and now resent. Say one honest preference each day for a week. Where to eat, what to watch, which option at work. Small ones count.

moon.upright:
The figure on this card has their back to a tree and three cups in front of them, and a Libra Moon's first worry would be whether it's rude not to pick one up. You need harmony to feel safe. Pleasant company, fairness, nobody upset with you. The card's Moon is the Cancer kind, square to Libra, which is friction that eventually forces a move, and in Libra the Moon is a guest with no standing, taking its lead from Venus. So the mood comes in as a kind of relationship tiredness. People have been a lot lately.

What it's like inside is that you want to withdraw and feel guilty for it. Libra Moons usually recharge through other people, a good conversation, being liked. Here the card is asking you to recharge alone, and your Moon doesn't really know how. Water and air are strangers to each other. The feeling side of this card and the social side of your Moon have to be introduced, and the introduction goes something like admitting you're not fine and that it isn't anybody's fault.

With a partner this shows up as saying yes to their plans and resenting it slightly. With friends it's the message you've read and haven't answered, with a draft you keep rewriting. In your body it can be tension in the lower back and a restless kind of tired. Spend one evening alone on purpose. Choose it, plan it, enjoy it if you can, and tell no one you're doing it.
moon.reversed:
This card reversed on a Libra Moon can look like hiding behind politeness. Everyone gets the nice version of you, and nobody gets the true one, because the true one is low and you've decided that's not fair on anyone. Venus, who the Moon answers to in Libra, keeps the surface smooth. Underneath, the resentment is building quietly, the square to Cancer grinding away.

It turns up with a partner as a coldness you'd deny if asked. With friends it's accepting every invitation and enjoying none of them. The Two of Swords decan is the Moon's piece of Libra, and it shows here as refusing to look at what you actually feel. Take the blindfold off for ten minutes. Write down how you honestly feel about the person you're most annoyed with, and don't show it to anyone.

rising.upright:
Libra rising has a way of making strangers feel comfortable. You smile, you mirror, you find common ground. The Four of Cups drawn for your mask means the charm is on a lower setting. You're still polite. You're just less interested in winning people over, and the square between Cancer and Libra shows up at first meetings as a tension between being nice and being honestly tired.

The Moon is a visitor in Libra, working under Venus, so your manners hold up. People might not even notice anything's wrong. But you'll feel it. The effort of the small talk, the smile held a few seconds too long, the relief when you get home. Air and water have to be introduced, and here your first impressions are being asked to let a bit more feeling show through. That's uncomfortable for an Ascendant built on grace. It can also be the most honest you've been with someone new in a while, and some people will warm to it.

At work it's the networking event where you stand at the edge instead of working the room. In dating it's being less agreeable than usual and finding out who likes you anyway. With new neighbours it's the wave instead of the chat. Let one new person see you a bit tired, a bit flat. Don't apologise for it.
rising.reversed:
Upside down on a Libra Ascendant, the card often shows as a pleasant face with nobody behind it. You go through the social motions perfectly, and people come away feeling they've met you when they haven't. Venus on your Ascendant keeps it gracious. The Two of Swords decan, the Moon's patch of Libra, adds a blindfold to it, and you're not quite seeing the people in front of you. It can also go the other way, a sudden coolness with people you've always been warm with.

This shows up when a new contact makes an offer and you're too busy being polite to hear it. Socially it's the event where you smiled at everyone and can't remember a single conversation. Next time you meet someone, stop and repeat back one thing they've said. It'll bring you back into the room.

sun.upright:
Scorpio and Cancer are trine, both water, four signs apart, and the element runs easily between them. That's the good news. The harder news is that the Moon is in fall in Scorpio. It's uncomfortable there and doesn't get heard properly, and it has to find an indirect way to do its job. For a Scorpio Sun, who's here to go deep, get to the truth and be known for having done it, the Four of Cups describes a stretch where the depth has gone murky and you can't see the bottom.

From the inside it's a brooding kind of withdrawal. The Cancer version of this card is soft and wants a blanket. Yours has an edge. You've gone quiet and you're watching. You've decided the three cups in front of you aren't worth it, and you've probably got reasons, and some of the reasons are good. The fall of the Moon means your feelings don't come out straight. They come out as suspicion, or a test, or a silence that's meant to mean something. Water on water amplifies all of this. It feels very private and very important.

At work it's the role you've mentally resigned from but still turn up to. With money it's hoarding, keeping what you've got close and not investing in anything new. In love it's a partner offering reassurance you won't take because you'd like to be sure first. Pick one offer you've been suspicious of. Take it at face value for a week and see what happens.
sun.reversed:
For a Scorpio Sun the reversed card is the withdrawal turned into a grudge. The Moon in fall already makes your feelings go the long way round, and upside down they stop coming out at all. You've decided nobody deserves to know what you think, and you'd sooner stay under the tree for good than admit you were hurt. Water sign, water card, so the feeling is enormous even when nothing shows.

It shows at work as a cold silence toward someone who let you down months ago, and in love as the long, loaded quiet your partner can't read. Money can go tight-fisted too. Say one direct sentence to the person you're freezing out. It can be short and it doesn't have to forgive them. It just has to be said out loud.

moon.upright:
A Scorpio Moon is the Moon in fall. It means your feelings run deep and don't come out in a straight line, and you learnt early to trust very few people with them. Now draw the Four of Cups, which is the Moon at home in Cancer, and put it on your tides. The two signs are trine, both water, and they understand each other perfectly. The card's Moon is comfortable. Yours never quite is. So what you're being shown is a version of withdrawal that could actually rest you, if you'd let it.

That's the hard part. When a Scorpio Moon pulls back, it usually does so to guard something, to watch, to lick a wound in private. This card's retreat is gentler, a rest after too much, with no enemy in it. You might find it odd to withdraw without a reason, without somebody to be wary of. Same element means the feeling is doubled, for good and for too much, and it can tip into brooding if you go in suspicious. Go in tired instead. That's probably the truth anyway.

In the body this can be heavy sleep, vivid dreams, a craving for being completely alone. With a partner it's needing space and not saying why, which to them looks like punishment. With family it's something old stirring, a feeling you'd sealed up. Tell the people close to you that you're resting, and that it isn't about them. Then rest.
moon.reversed:
Upside down on a Scorpio Moon, this card can turn a rest into a siege. The Moon in fall already struggles to say what it feels, and reversed, it stops trying. You sit with a hurt until it hardens. Someone offers comfort and you look for the catch. The quiet goes on long enough that people stop knocking.

It shows in sleep that's broken by the same thoughts going round, and in a jealousy or suspicion you know is bigger than the facts. A partner may feel shut out and not know how they got there. Water on water, so it's all very large and very silent. Pick the one person you trust most and tell them the smallest true piece of what's going on. They'll probably be relieved you did.

rising.upright:
Scorpio rising doesn't give much away on a first meeting, and people tend to feel a bit examined. Drawing this card for the mask pushes that further. You're more guarded than usual, harder to read, and your first impressions come with the arms crossed. The card's Moon is in fall in Scorpio. It doesn't get to speak plainly on your doorway, so whatever you're feeling comes across as reserve, or intensity, or a stare that goes on a moment too long.

The trine from Cancer helps. Both water, the same element, and the card's softness gets through to people who are paying attention. The ones who stick around past the first ten minutes will find you surprisingly gentle. The trouble is how many don't. Mars rules Scorpio, and a Mars-ruled Ascendant that's withdrawn looks like it's got something against you. You probably haven't. You're tired, and you're deciding who's safe, and your face is doing it out loud.

At a new job it's colleagues who think you're judging them. In dating it's the other person trying hard and not knowing if you're interested. With a new friend it's the long pause before you answer anything personal. Give one person the benefit of the doubt early. Tell them something small and true about yourself in the first conversation. Watch how they respond.
rising.reversed:
Scorpio rising under this card reversed can seem impossible to reach. You've pulled so far back that people meeting you only get the wall. The Moon in fall on your Ascendant keeps the feeling underground, and reversed, it can look like contempt when it's really caution that's gone too far. Friends who know you know the warmth is in there. Strangers don't get that far.

At work it's the new manager who writes you off as difficult. In a new friendship it's the person who reached out twice and then gave up. On a date it's the guardedness that reads as disinterest. Soften one thing on purpose next time. Smile first, or ask the first question, or say you're nervous if you are. People tend to meet that halfway.

sun.upright:
Sagittarius Suns are built for the next horizon, and they like to be seen heading for it. What this card shows is someone sitting under a tree who's lost interest in going anywhere. Cancer and Sagittarius are quincunx, five signs apart, with nothing in common, and the only way to live with a quincunx is constant small adjustment. The Moon is a guest in your sign with no rank, taking its lead from Jupiter, which is why even your flat patches tend to be about meaning. It isn't just that you're bored. It's that you've started wondering what any of it is for.

Fire and water are opposed. This card is water, and it's damping the part of you that usually gets up and goes. That can be frightening for a Sagittarius Sun, because enthusiasm is so much of who you think you are. There's another thread worth knowing. The Moon rules the middle ten degrees of Sagittarius, the decan of the Nine of Wands, the card of holding on when you're worn out. If your Sun falls there, you'll know this state well, the weariness after a long stretch of hanging in, and a suspicion of anything new being offered.

At work it's the big plan you pitched last year that feels like somebody else's idea. With study or travel it's the course or the trip you've stopped mentioning. With friends it's being less fun than usual and worrying that's all they liked you for. Let the flatness be here without deciding what it means. Give it a fortnight before you draw any big conclusions about your life.
sun.reversed:
Upturned for a Sagittarius Sun, this card can look like restlessness pretending to be freedom. You've gone flat, and instead of sitting with it you book something, quit something, or announce a new philosophy of life. Jupiter, colouring the Moon here, makes the escape large. None of it touches the feeling, which comes along in your luggage. The quincunx between the card's sign and yours means none of this fits neatly, and you keep adjusting when you could be resting.

The other version is cynicism. You decide nothing is worth believing in and say so, often, a bit loudly. It shows up with friends who've stopped bringing you their enthusiasms, and at work as dismissing ideas before they're finished. Before the next big move, stay put for two weeks. Do the ordinary things. Notice what you're actually trying to leave behind.

moon.upright:
A Sagittarius Moon needs room, a plan for something good ahead, and people who don't hold it too tightly. The card drawn for your tides is almost the opposite mood. It's the Cancer Moon, at home and wanting to stay put, meeting yours across a quincunx, two signs with nothing in common that have to keep making small adjustments to get along. In Sagittarius the Moon has no special dignity and takes on Jupiter's appetite for more. So when this card lands, the appetite goes missing, and you might not recognise yourself.

What you'll notice is that the usual cures don't work. The trip you'd normally plan doesn't appeal. The new book sits unopened. Water and fire are opposed elements, and water is winning this one, so the fire that keeps your spirits up has been damped. Sagittarius Moons often cope with feeling by finding the bigger picture, the lesson in it, the silver lining. This card is asking you to skip the lesson for once and just be a bit sad, or a bit bored, without making it mean anything.

In the body it shows as restlessness with no energy behind it, legs that want to move and a body that won't. With a partner it's feeling hemmed in and not being able to say by what. With a friend it's the long voice note you didn't answer. Give yourself one slow, local day. Walk somewhere near home you've never walked. Don't plan the next adventure while you're doing it.
moon.reversed:
The card upside down on a Sagittarius Moon often shows as a mood you keep outrunning. You're busy, you're cheerful in public, and the flat feeling catches up at night. Jupiter, the Moon's host in your sign, makes the running feel optimistic, and it keeps you from ever landing. The Nine of Wands, the Moon's own decan in Sagittarius, adds a guardedness, so when someone gets close to the low bit, you get defensive. Fire sign, water card, and they never quite settle.

Friends see the bright surface and not much else. A partner may feel held at arm's length. Sleep gets late and restless. Tell one person that you've been lower than you've let on. Say it plainly, and stay in the conversation for the next five minutes without making a joke.

rising.upright:
Sagittarius rising walks in ready for anything, friendly, open, laughing at something before the introductions are over. With this card drawn for your mask, the doorway goes quiet. People who know you will find you less bouncy, and strangers will meet a more reserved version of you, somebody who's watching the room instead of taking it over. The Moon is a visitor on a Sagittarius Ascendant, taking Jupiter's colour, so it still has some warmth. But the Cancer water in this card is opposed to your fire, and the first thing it puts out is the easy enthusiasm.

The quincunx between Cancer and Sagittarius makes that awkward. Nothing about the two fits, so you're constantly adjusting, trying to be your usual self and finding it doesn't quite come. The Moon's decan in your sign is the Nine of Wands, the card of being worn down and still on guard, and that's a good description of how you might be coming across. Tired, a bit wary of new offers, a little quicker to say no than usual. That's not the end of the world. Some people will find you easier to reach like this, because you're not performing.

On a first date it's being more honest than usual about what you actually want. In a job interview it's less charm and a steadier answer. When travelling it's the day you stay in the hostel and let the others go. When you meet someone new, let them see the quieter version for a while. Watch who stays interested.
rising.reversed:
Sagittarius rising with the card turned over can come across as distracted or dismissive. You're half there. People tell you about their plans and you look past them, and the Jupiter-coloured Moon on your Ascendant makes the boredom easy to read. Or you swing the other way and turn the charm up to cover the flatness, too loud, too many jokes, promises you won't keep. Fire meeting water can look like steam, a lot of noise and not much heat.

At work it shows in new colleagues who feel brushed off. In friendship it's the plan you agreed to with great enthusiasm and quietly dropped. On a date it's looking at your phone. Put the phone away at the next first meeting. Ask the other person about something they care about and stay with it for a proper while.

sun.upright:
Capricorn sits directly opposite Cancer, and the Moon, which rules Cancer, is in detriment in Capricorn. That means it has to work against the grain here, and you can see the effort. For a Capricorn Sun, who's here to build something that lasts and be respected for it, this card is Cancer's end of your own axis showing up uninvited. The need to stop, rest and be looked after. You're not great at any of those, and you know it.

From the inside it's the flatness that comes after achievement. You've climbed the thing, got the role, paid off the debt, and it doesn't feel how you thought it would. Three cups lined up, all earned, none of them doing much. An opposition is a pull toward balance, and the balance your chart is being asked for is a bit of Cancer. Home, family, rest, feeling. Water and earth get on well, so this isn't a crisis. It's a slow, damp season where things can grow if you let them. The trouble is the Moon in detriment makes it hard to ask for care, and you'd sooner push through.

At work it's staring at a promotion you wanted and feeling nothing. With family it's the parent or child you've been meaning to spend proper time with. With your body it's the tiredness you've been treating as a scheduling problem. Take one full day off with no work at all, and don't make up for it later. Spend part of it at home, doing nothing useful.
sun.reversed:
For a Capricorn Sun this card reversed usually means the flatness has been filed under work and ignored. The Moon in detriment already struggles in your sign, and upside down it goes quiet altogether. You keep performing, keep producing, and feel less and less. People around you may only notice that you've become short with them. The opposition to Cancer means the need for care is right there on your own axis, and you're standing with your back to it.

At home it can look like being present in body and absent in every other way. At work it's the grim competence of someone who's stopped caring and won't admit it. The offer being missed is usually rest, or help, from someone who's noticed. Say yes to the next offer of help you'd normally refuse. Let them see you need it.

moon.upright:
The Moon is in detriment in Capricorn, and if you've got a Capricorn Moon you probably know what that means in practice. Feelings get handled. You cope, you manage, you do what needs doing, and the crying happens later, alone, if at all. Drawing the Four of Cups onto a Capricorn Moon puts the Moon at home, in Cancer, across from the Moon struggling in your sign. It's the same planet at opposite ends of the same axis, and the card is showing you what your Moon might need if it ever got to rest.

That's uncomfortable. The card's mood is withdrawal, a pause, a heaviness that won't be pushed. A Capricorn Moon's first move with a heavy feeling is to organise it. Make a plan, get more sleep, sort it out. Earth and water are good partners, and your earth can hold this water well enough, but only if you stop trying to drain it. You may find yourself unusually tired, oddly tearful at small things, or less willing to carry everyone. That's the Cancer end of the axis asking for its share.

In the body it's the tight shoulders and the teeth ground at night. With a parent, especially a strict one, it can be an old ache about not being comforted. With a partner it's tensing up when they offer a hug. Let one person look after you in a small, practical way. A meal cooked for you counts. Don't thank them by doing something back straight away.
moon.reversed:
Upside down, this card on a Capricorn Moon can mean you've frozen the feeling solid. The Moon in detriment was already working hard to be heard, and reversed, you've decided feelings are a luxury. It looks like strength. It's mostly exhaustion that's been told to wait. Earth holds water well, which is exactly why you can carry this for so long without anyone seeing.

It shows up at home as a coldness you don't intend, and with a partner as the conversation you keep saying you'll have when things calm down. Your body will eventually insist, a cold you can't shake, sleep that stops working. Before that happens, take one evening off from coping. Tell someone you're tired and let them handle dinner.

rising.upright:
Capricorn rising already comes across as serious, capable and slightly hard to get to know. With this card drawn for your mask, the reserve goes up a notch. The Moon is in detriment on a Capricorn Ascendant, working against the grain, and the Cancer softness the card carries doesn't show easily through your front. People meet a composed, tired, faintly unimpressed person, and they may assume you don't rate them.

With Capricorn rising, Cancer is the sign opposite your Ascendant, the one on your seventh house, the house of partners. So the card is really describing a tension between how you present and what you want from other people. You'd like to be looked after for once. You're presenting as someone who's never needed it. The opposition pulls toward balance, and the balance here is letting a bit of that need show at the start of things, in first meetings, before you've established yourself as the reliable one. Earth and water are friendly. It's safer to be soft than you think.

At a new workplace it's being handed responsibility on day one because you look like you can take it, and taking it though you're tired. In dating it's the other person wondering if you're even interested. With neighbours or new friends it's being respected long before you're liked. Let somebody new help you with something small, carrying a box, a recommendation, a lift. Accept it without insisting you're fine.
rising.reversed:
Capricorn rising with this card reversed can look forbidding. You've closed up so far that people meeting you only see the professional shell, efficient, polite, cold. The Moon in detriment on your Ascendant, turned over, drops the last bit of warmth from the front. You might be quite lonely behind it. Cancer sits on your seventh house, so partners are where the missing warmth gets noticed first.

At work it shows as the new team keeping a respectful distance. Socially it's the invitation that dries up because you looked like you'd rather not. In a new relationship it's being admired and not approached. Next time you meet someone, tell them one thing that isn't about your work. A hobby, a pet, where you grew up. Something small with some warmth in it.

sun.upright:
Aquarius Suns want to be free to think their own thoughts and to be seen as a bit different, a bit ahead. The card drawn for your light is the most private card in the suit, somebody sitting by themselves with their arms crossed. Cancer and Aquarius are quincunx, five signs apart with nothing in common, and the two keep having to adjust around each other. The Moon has no special place in your sign. It visits, taking its colour from Saturn, your traditional ruler, or Uranus if you use the modern one, and that gives even your low moods a detached, slightly cool quality.

From the inside it's a kind of alienation. The group you usually belong to, the cause, the friends, the project, feels flat. You look at it from the outside and think, is this really it. Water and air are neutral to each other, they need an introduction, and the introduction here is between your ideas about how you feel and the actual feeling. The Moon also rules the last ten degrees of Aquarius, the decan of the Seven of Swords, which is the card of doing things alone and in secret. Late Aquarius Suns especially may find they've been quietly keeping their dissatisfaction to themselves.

At work it's the team you've stopped contributing to. Among friends it's the chat thread where you've gone silent, and nobody's asked why. In love it's feeling more alone with your partner than without them. Tell one friend you've been feeling disconnected. Don't dress it up as a theory about society.
sun.reversed:
An Aquarius Sun with the card upside down can go cold and superior about it. You've withdrawn, and you've decided it's because everyone else is dull. Saturn, colouring the Moon in Aquarius, makes the distance feel principled. It isn't always. Sometimes you're hurt and haven't said. Fixed air holds a position once it's taken, including the position that you're fine on your own.

The Seven of Swords is the Moon's decan in your sign, and it shows here as keeping plans and feelings to yourself, doing things around people instead of with them. At work it's working alone and resenting that nobody helps. With friends it's disappearing without explanation. Pick one person you've drifted from and send them something warm and specific. A memory, a link, a thing that made you think of them.

moon.upright:
An Aquarius Moon needs space and a bit of distance to feel safe. You process feelings by stepping back and looking at them, and too much closeness too fast makes you edgy. Drawing this card for your tides might seem like a match, because the card is about withdrawing. But the card's withdrawal is the Cancer kind, warm, wet and wanting comfort, and yours is the cool kind. Cancer and Aquarius sit a quincunx apart, nothing in common, and the Moon's only visiting your sign, where it takes on Saturn's reserve.

So there's a mismatch. You're pulling back, and you'd normally feel fine in your own space, and you don't. Something about this retreat is lonelier than usual. That's the Cancer water getting in, the need for someone to actually hold you, which an Aquarius Moon doesn't always admit to. Air and water don't clash, but they don't know each other either, and the feeling may come out sideways. As a sudden irritation with friends. As a strong opinion about something that isn't really the issue.

With a partner it's asking for space and then feeling abandoned when you get it. With friends it's reacting to every message in the group chat and turning down every invite. Your body carries it as nervous tiredness and trouble switching off at night. Ask one person for something specific and close. A phone call, a hug, an hour on the couch. Tell them you asked because you needed it.
moon.reversed:
Turned over on an Aquarius Moon, the card can harden the distance into a policy. Saturn, who hosts the Moon in Aquarius, is good at walls. You tell yourself you don't need anybody, and you're convincing. The feeling behind it, which is mostly a hurt about being left out, goes somewhere very quiet. The Seven of Swords decan, the Moon's slice of your sign, adds a habit of handling everything alone and privately, so nobody even knows there's something to help with.

It shows up as friendships that fade because you stopped replying, and as a partner who feels they're living with a flatmate. Sleep can go strange, late and wired. Pick the friend you miss most. Tell them so, in those words, even if it feels awkward to type.

rising.upright:
Aquarius rising already comes across as friendly and a little apart, interested in everyone, attached to no one in particular. Draw this card for an Aquarius Ascendant and the apart bit is what people notice first. The Moon visits your rising sign without any dignity of its own and takes on Saturn's coolness, so your withdrawal shows as detachment. You seem to be watching from the edge, a bit amused, a bit elsewhere.

The quincunx between Cancer and Aquarius means the card's softness doesn't get through easily. It has to be translated. You may actually be feeling quite tender, lonely even, and none of it's reaching your face. Strangers see someone independent and assume you're fine. The Moon's decan in Aquarius is the Seven of Swords, the card of going it alone, and there's a streak of that in how you're meeting people. Doing it yourself, not asking, slipping out of the party without saying goodbye. It protects you. It also means the people who'd like to get closer don't know how.

At work it's being seen as the independent one, left to get on with it when you'd quite like some company. At a gathering it's the conversation you have with one person on the balcony, the only real one of the night. On a date it's being interesting and hard to read. Say one warm, uncomplicated thing to the next new person you meet. Tell them you're glad they came, or that you like their jacket, and mean it.
rising.reversed:
An Aquarius Ascendant with the card turned over can come across as aloof to the point of rudeness. You're elsewhere, and people can tell. Saturn's reserve on the Moon here turns detachment into a kind of chill, and new people read it as you having judged them. Or you go the other way and get contrary, arguing a point just to keep people at a distance. The quincunx means your feelings and your face aren't lined up, and people only see the face.

At work this is the colleague who's decided you don't like them. Socially it's the group that stops inviting you because you always leave first. Online it's the sharp reply that ends a conversation. At the next first meeting, stay to the end. Help clear up, or walk someone to the station, and let yourself be part of it for once.

sun.upright:
Pisces Suns are here to feel their way through life and be known for their imagination and their kindness. The Four of Cups comes to you in your own element. Cancer and Pisces are trine, both water, four signs apart, and they flow into each other easily. The Moon has no special dignity in Pisces. It's a visitor, taking its colour from Jupiter, or Neptune if you use the modern ruler, which makes it dreamy and wide open here, and a little hard to pin down.

Same element means the card speaks your language and turns the volume up, for better and for too much. The better part is that you know how to retreat. You know how to lie on the floor with music on and let a mood pass through. The too much is that Pisces can drift. The three cups on the grass are real things, the job, the art, the people, and you can find yourself looking at them from a long way off, as if through water, unable to decide which one to pick up, so you pick up none. It feels peaceful. After a while it feels like being stuck.

At work it's the creative project that's been paused so long it's gone cold. With money it's bills left unopened because opening them would break the spell. In love it's a partner offering something real, a plan, a holiday, a promise, and you not quite registering it. Pick one of the three cups and use it properly for a week. Finish one thing you started.
sun.reversed:
A Pisces Sun with this card upside down may have drifted a long way out. The retreat felt healing at first, and then it became the only place you wanted to be. Jupiter, and Neptune for modern astrologers, widen the Moon's reach in your sign, and reversed, that can mean losing track of time, of plans, of people waiting to hear from you. Water on water deepens the pull, so getting back needs something solid.

It shows in the unanswered messages, the half-finished work, the sense that life is going on somewhere else. It can also show as escape, too much screen, too much sleep, too much of whatever helps you check out. Set one small anchor each day for a week. A walk at the same time, a call to the same friend, one task done before lunch.

moon.upright:
The Moon in Pisces is the most porous Moon there is. You soak up other people's moods, and you need regular time alone to wring them back out. This card for your tides is that time alone. The Cancer Moon of the card meets your Pisces Moon across a trine, water to water, easy and familiar, so the retreat it describes is one you know how to take. Jupiter hosts the Moon in your sign, which adds a boundless quality, feelings that don't have edges.

The same element amplifies, though, and that's the thing to watch. A Cancer retreat has walls. It's a shell, a home, a door that shuts. A Pisces retreat has no walls at all, and it can turn into drifting, a vague sadness that you can't trace back to anything. From the inside it feels like being underwater on a calm day. Quiet and not unpleasant, but you can't hear anyone properly, and people offering help sound far away.

Sleep goes long and dreamy, and the mornings are heavy. With a partner it's the evening you're present and somewhere else. With friends it's missing the kindness they're offering because you're too far in. Borrow the Cancer habit of walls. Choose a room, a time, a start and an end for your retreat, and come out when the time's up.
moon.reversed:
This card upside down on a Pisces Moon can mean the retreat has lost its edges altogether. You've gone so far into the mood that it's become the weather you live in, and the Jupiter and Neptune side of your Moon makes it feel almost pleasant, like floating. People reaching for you can't find you. Water meeting water, the pull is strong and familiar, which is why it's so easy to stay.

You'll see it in sleep that runs long and doesn't refresh, in a messy house, in friends who've stopped expecting replies. A partner might feel like they're caring for someone who isn't quite there. Ask one person to check in on you every day for a week, by text, at a fixed time. Answer them every time, even if it's a single word.

rising.upright:
Pisces rising meets the world softly. A gentle manner, a faraway look, a way of taking on the tone of whoever's in front of you. With this card for your mask, the faraway look is doing most of the talking. The Moon is only a guest on a Pisces Ascendant, answering to Jupiter, or Neptune for modern astrologers, and it makes the withdrawal hazy. People aren't meeting a closed door. They're meeting fog.

Cancer is trine to Pisces, water to water, so the card's mood sits naturally on you, and the amplifying works both ways. The good side is that people find you peaceful to be around, unthreatening, easy to talk to without much being asked back. The harder side is that you're not really taking anything in. Somebody introduces themselves and you forget their name before they've finished. Somebody offers you a lead, a job, a number, and it drifts off. It's a very pleasant kind of absence.

In a new role at work it's being liked and being forgotten when it counts. On a date it's the other person talking and you nodding somewhere else. At a party it's the kitchen, or the garden, alone with a drink and a cat. When you meet someone new, write their name down afterwards, and one thing they said. Follow up on the thing.
rising.reversed:
Pisces rising with this card reversed can come across as vague to the point of being unreliable. The fog around your Ascendant thickens, and people meeting you can't tell whether you've agreed to anything. The Moon, taking Neptune's colours here, blurs the edges of every first meeting. Some people will fill the gap with their own ideas about you, and not all of them will be kind. Water on water means the mood is strong and feels normal to you, so you might not notice it.

At work it's the new contact who thinks you're flaky. Socially it's the plan you said yes to and forgot. In dating it's the other person projecting a whole story onto your silence. Be more definite than feels natural at the next first meeting. Say what you want, or say no, and make the follow-up happen.

1.upright:
The first house is the body you walk around in and the way you start things. Its natural sign is Aries and its natural ruler is Mars, so this corner of the chart likes to move first and ask later. Drop the Four of Cups in here and you've got a Moon card in a Mars house, Cancer square to Aries, water poured on a fire that's used to being lit. The first house is angular, one of the four corners of the chart, so whatever lands here shows. People will see it on you.

What you'll feel is a reluctance to start. The engine turns over and doesn't catch. You get up, you look at the day, and the usual first moves don't appeal. The square between Cancer and Aries is friction that eventually forces action, and in the meantime it feels like two instincts arguing, one saying go and one saying stay in bed. Your posture might change. People may ask if you're all right when you think you look normal.

With your body it's the gym bag that hasn't been unpacked and the walk you keep meaning to take. With how you present, it's wearing the comfortable clothes, the hood up, the hair not quite done. In new situations it's letting others lead. Let the body set the pace for a while. Walk slowly somewhere green, most days, and notice when you feel like speeding up.
1.reversed:
Flipped in the first house, this card can mean the retreat has started to show on you in ways you haven't chosen. Mars, the house's natural ruler, doesn't like being idle, and when a fire house is kept damp too long it gets irritable. You might be short with people, restless in your own skin, snapping at small things. Cancer squares Aries, and the tension has to go somewhere.

The other way it shows is a sudden overcorrection, the new haircut, the new regime, the big announcement, all started at once and dropped within days. The body usually wants something in between. Choose one physical thing that gets you out of the house most days, a swim, a walk, a bike ride to the shop. Keep it small enough that you'll actually keep doing it.

2.upright:
Money and what you think you're worth sit in the second house, and this is one of the friendlier places for this card to land. The house's natural sign is Taurus, where the Moon is exalted, so a Moon card is welcomed here, treated as an honoured guest. Cancer and Taurus are sextile, water and earth, elements that hold each other up. The second house is succedent, the part of the chart that builds up and keeps.

The friction is quieter than that. The Moon exalted in Taurus is the planet at its most idealised, and what it idealises here is feeling safe with what you've got. When this card lands in the money house, the idea of security and the feeling of it come apart. You check the balance and it's fine, and you don't feel fine. Or you get paid well for something and it doesn't register as proof you're any good. It isn't a money problem so much as a worth problem, and those two live in the same house for a reason.

With money it's being careful to the point of joyless, or spending on things you don't much want. With self-worth it's doubting whether what you do is valued, even when the evidence says it is. At work it can be an offer of more pay or a better deal that you haven't properly looked at. Go through what you own and pick three things you actually love. Use them. Then find the offer you've been ignoring and read it properly.
2.reversed:
